correctness.rationale: From the complete graph condition, a face uses fewer than t graph parts. The H-fixed affine point has equal coordinates on every H-vertex orbit, hence is the orbit-union complex; an H-vertex orbit meets exactly every graph part in one H-part orbit. All vertex orbits above that part orbit are interchangeable, and collapsing them to one representative is a simplicial map contiguous to the identity because the total occupied graph parts remain unchanged. The resulting scalar threshold complex has weights w_j=number of parts in each part orbit, faces of total weight ≤T=t−1. If its smallest weight exceeds T it has empty realization. Otherwise its minimum-weight-vertex closed star A is contractible. Any face S outside A has weight T−w_min < w(S)≤T, and every proper subface has weight at most T−w_min, so it lies in A. The quotient by the star is a wedge of a sphere S^{|S|−1} for each such S; the quotient map is a homotopy equivalence. A simplex case t>m, dimension-zero wedge, and empty fixed locus are handled. The example weights (1,1,1,2,2), t=5 give two S² and one S¹, and the ambient trivial-action weights (1^7) give C(6,4)=15 spheres S³. The identical proof is corroborated by the independently inspected broader published affine retraction theorem. An independently authored finite diagnostic directly constructs H-orbit faces and mod-2 reduced homology for 305 cases (21,009 such faces) and the seven-part example, which corroborate but do not prove the unrestricted statement.
residual_risks: The finite independent checks verify only bounded graph sizes and mod-2 homology; integer homotopy type follows from the complete star quotient proof.
No normalizer-equivariant compatible wedge decomposition, naturality under subgroup inclusions, or extension beyond finite complete multipartite graphs is established.

value.rationale: The topic (classification of genuine subgroup fixed points rather than vertexwise-fixed subcomplexes) is mathematically meaningful. However the submitted entire classification, its mixed-dimensional example, and every asserted exact invariant are already supplied by a more general published equivariant-compression theorem. There is no genuinely independent structural lemma, new boundary, classification or unknown invariant left after taking the known implication. The standalone quota wedge proof is the classical Pakianathan–Winfree theorem, and the assigned action-to-weight reduction is also covered. As an original new mathematical contribution this is a duplicate of known coverage, not a valuable surviving claim.
residual_risks: The intrinsic subject remains valuable; this FAIL concerns absence of additional mathematical value in the audited claimed contribution, not the worth of fixed-point topology itself.
Same-day publication metadata prevents an assertion about which team independently discovered the argument first.

limitations: The accepted correctness conclusion is about finite complete multipartite graphs, integer t≥2, and arbitrary graph-automorphism subgroups; no normalizer-equivariant splitting follows.
The definite scientific rejection is for published all-domain theorem-level overlap, not for mathematical incorrectness. Publication chronology within November 8 is unestablished.
